intended_object: The canonical inclusion morphism N ↪ R_u(G) of a connected normal smooth unipotent closed subgroup N (a "candidate", given by a Hopf ideal I) into the k-unipotent radical of a finite-type affine group G over a field k (docstring, module doc, companion compatibility lemma).
explanation: The body applies `CommHopfAlgCat.quotientSpecMapOfLe` to the inclusion `unipotentRadicalDefiningIdeal H ≤ I` given by `unipotentRadicalDefiningIdeal_le`. `quotientSpecMapOfLe` sends I ≤ J to the group-scheme morphism Spec(H/J) ⟶ Spec(H/I), obtained by applying hopfSpec to the quotient map H/I → H/J. With J = I (the candidate) and the radical's ideal in the role of I, this gives Spec(H/I) ⟶ Spec(H/radical ideal), which is the closed-subgroup inclusion N → R_u(G). The companion lemma confirms that composing it with the radical's inclusion into G gives N's own inclusion into G, so it is the canonical (unique, since closed immersions are monomorphisms) inclusion. The field and finite-type setting is the one in which the k-unipotent radical is defined, so the definition is not too narrow. Mathlib has no unipotent radical.
